subject: Medicine
summary: Pyelonephritis is an infection of the kidney’s collecting system, usually ascending from the bladder. It presents with fever, flank pain and urinary symptoms, and requires prompt antibiotics and supportive care.

sections.p: Acute pyelonephritis is a bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma and pelvis, most often caused by E. coli ascending from the bladder. Diagnosis combines clinical features, urine culture and imaging when available.

sections.p: Severity is graded by clinical stability and organ dysfunction. Mild disease is managed outpatient; moderate to severe requires inpatient care and monitoring for sepsis.
b: Mild: fever, flank pain, no systemic signs
Severe: septic shock, acute kidney injury

sections.p: The most common cause is ascending E. coli infection. Other bacteria include Klebsiella, Proteus, and in low‑resource settings, organisms linked to HIV, TB, or malaria.
Patients report fever, chills, flank pain, and urinary urgency. In children, symptoms may be nonspecific, with irritability and poor feeding.
Tests confirm infection, identify the organism, and assess severity. When resources are limited, clinical judgment and basic labs guide treatment.

sections.p: Severe sepsis, hypotension, oliguria, or sudden worsening of pain require urgent care. Complications include abscess, sepsis, and chronic kidney disease.

faq.q: What if the patient has HIV?
faq.a: HIV increases risk; treat with broad‑spectrum antibiotics and monitor for opportunistic infections.
